56035.text: Most of Sublette County's cropland is irrigated, 97 percent, and water comes mostly from surface sources. Non-irrigated ground rents for $21 per acre now, up 40 percent from 2013, while irrigated ground is $30 per acre. Land value is $2,038 per acre and has climbed 4.3 percent a year from 2017 to 2022. CRP acres total 18300, or 17.5 percent of the cropland base.

56037.text: Most of Sweetwater County's cropland is irrigated, drawing mainly from surface water. July nights have warmed 0.59 degrees Fahrenheit per decade since 1976, reaching an average low of 52.3 degrees Fahrenheit in 2017-2026 versus a 1991-2020 normal of 50.9 degrees Fahrenheit. Non-irrigated rent ran $32 per acre in 2026; irrigated rent was $44 per acre. Land value rose 30.7 percent from 2017 to 2022.

56045.text: Heat and drought have driven the crop insurance losses here. From 2000 to 2009, heat and drought made up 29 percent of indemnities paid. That share rose to 74 percent in 2010-2019 and stayed at 67 percent in 2020-2025. The loss ratio for all closed crop years from 1989 to 2025 was 1.32, meaning the county paid out $1.32 in indemnities for every dollar of premium collected. Non-irrigated cash rent was $17 per acre in 2023, up 25.9 percent since 2012. The census value of land and buildings was $953 per acre in 2022.
